items.title: Malaysia's online job vacancies surge 17.8pct to 654,655 in Q3
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysia's online job offerings has risen 17.8 per cent to 654,655 in the third quarter (Q3) of 2026, with advertising and marketing professionals recording the highest demand among occupations. Technicians and associate professionals recorded 110,180 job offerings, followed by managers with 96,442. Among individual occupations, advertising and marketing professionals topped the list with 44,989 job offerings.

items.title: Negri Sembilan Palace: Ismail's resignation as MB yet to be verified
items.summary: SEREMBAN: The Negri Sembilan Palace has taken note of the statement by Barisan Nasional secretary-general Datuk Seri Dr Zambry Abdul Kadir regarding Datuk Ismail Lasim's resignation menteri besar. However, the Secretary of the Royal Household, in a statement today, said the Palace had yet to verify the authenticity of the letter, which Zambry said had been signed by Ismail. Yesterday, Zambry had said Ismail had submitted a resignation letter to Tuanku Muhriz.

items.title: No sticker, but don’t forget to renew: JPJ seized 35,555 vehicles over expired road tax since 2023
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 17 — The Road Transport Department (JPJ) has seized 35,555 vehicles since 2023 for being driven with expired motor vehicle licences (LKM) or road tax, the Dewan Rakyat was told today. The Transport Ministry (MOT) said 1,608,238 P22 summons notices were also issued during the same period to motorists caught driving vehicles with expired road tax. The ministry said enforcement officers could verify road tax validity digitally through JPJ’s system, while action could be taken under the Road Transport Act 1987 against those driving vehicles with expired road tax on public roads.

items.title: Wangsa Maju LRT crowding sparks passenger complaints
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Crowding at Wangsa Maju LRT station today led to the closure of an escalator, with commuters claiming they had to wait up to 15 minutes to access the platform. In a post on Threads, one commuter said there had been no warning despite the growing crowds. "Wangsa Maju LRT is so packed that they had to close the escalator.

items.title: Flood damage cost Selangor RM52.9m last year, more than double the 2024 figure
items.summary: SHAH ALAM, Nov 17 — Flood losses in Selangor rose to RM52.9 million in 2025 from RM22.6 million the previous year, said Youth, Sports and Entrepreneurship Committee chairman Mohd Najwan Halimi. Citing the Selangor State Flood Loss Value Statistics for 2024 and 2025 compiled by the Department of Statistics Malaysia (DOSM) Selangor, he said the losses comprised RM15.3 million in damage to residences, RM4 million to vehicles and RM1 million to business premises. Mohd Najwan said agricultural losses and infrastructure damage stood at RM9.6 million and RM26.6 million, respectively.

items.title: Marcos wants Asean, East Asia to turn commitments into food, energy security
items.summary: MANILA: President Ferdinand R. Marcos Jr. on Tuesday urged Southeast Asian and East Asian leaders to translate regional cooperation into concrete safeguards for food and energy supplies, stressing that global disruptions must not leave households facing higher costs and businesses struggling to operate, The Philippine News Agency (PNA) reported. In opening the 29th Asean Plus Three (APT) Summit, Marcos said the impact of conflicts, supply disruptions and other shocks thousands of miles away can quickly reach East and Southeast Asia through rising rice prices, energy costs and lost income. The Asean Plus Three framework brings together the 11 Asean member states and China, Japan and South Korea.

items.title: 11 men arrested after Sandakan market clash
items.summary: SANDAKAN: Police have arrested 11 men in connection with a clash between two groups at Pasar Bandar Ramai-Ramai in Sandakan last night. Sandakan police chief Assistant Commissioner George Abd Rakman said police received information through the emergency hotline about the clash, which was believed to have involved sharp weapons. © New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

items.title: RTD: Many VIPs, influencers driving luxury vehicles without insurance, road tax
items.summary: ALOR STAR: VIPs and social media influencers were among those detained by the Kedah Road Transport Department for driving luxury vehicles without valid road tax and insurance coverage. State RTD director Stien Van Lutam said some of them gave excuses such as forgetting to renew their insurance, while others claimed to own too many vehicles. He said some resorted to such actions due to financial difficulties and being blacklisted, yet continued to flaunt their wealth by driving luxury vehicles daily.

items.title: Body of man with star-shaped tattoo found floating in river
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The body of a man with a star-shaped tattoo on the right side of his neck was found floating in a river near Kampung Merbau Sempak, Sungai Buloh, on Friday. Sungai Buloh police chief Superintendent Mohd Hafiz Muhammad Nor said police were alerted to the discovery by the public about 9.35am. The body of the heavyset man was found without a shirt, wearing only blue jeans and socks," he said in a statement yesterday.

items.title: Achi Jaya takes over Boustead Plantations for RM4.3bil?
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The Armed Forces Fund Board (LTAT) has chosen Achi Jaya Plantations Sdn Bhd to take over Boustead Plantations Bhd (BPlant) at an estimated price of RM4.3 billion, sources told Berita Harian. Achi Jaya is understood to have beaten SD Guthrie Bhd and Tradewinds Plantation Bhd for the takeover, two companies with larger-scale plantation operations. Of this, 557,258 hectares comprise oil palm planted areas, including 292,122 hectares in Malaysia.

items.title: Over 13,000 deepfakes taken down since 2024, including 1,178 targeting political leaders, Parliament told
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 17 — Platform providers removed 13,883 deepfake items between January 1, 2024, and October 31 this year following takedown requests by the Malaysian Communications and Multimedia Commission (MCMC) based on public complaints, Communications Minister Datuk Fahmi Fadzil told Parliament today. Of these, 1,178 items involved political leaders, Fahmi said when outlining regulatory and enforcement measures against artificial intelligence (AI) misuse. On enforcement, Fahmi said the MCMC investigated 61 cases involving AI misuse under Section 233 of the Communications and Multimedia Act 1998 (Act 588) between January 1, 2025, and October 31 this year.

items.title: Anwar welcomes Macron at historic Dataran Merdeka ceremony
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 17 — French President Emmanuel Macron, on a two-day official visit to Malaysia beginning yesterday, was accorded a state welcome at Dataran Merdeka here this morning. Macron, accompanied by his wife Brigitte Macron, arrived at 9.30 am and was received by Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim and his wife, Datin Seri Dr Wan Azizah Wan Ismail. Also present were both Deputy Prime Ministers, Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi and Datuk Seri Fadillah Yusof.

items.title: Saifuddin: No dedicated digital map of illegal border routes, high-risk areas
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Authorities have identified 443 illegal routes and 281 hotspots used by smugglers since January. However, Home Minister Datuk Seri Saifuddin Nasution Ismail said enforcement agencies do not yet have a dedicated digital geospatial map of these locations. "At present, the border security enforcement agencies do not yet have a dedicated digital geospatial data map that records in detail the locations of illegal routes, high-risk areas, control weak points or locations needing immediate security intervention.

items.title: United Airlines resolves technology issue that disrupted departing flights
items.summary: WASHINGTON: United Airlines said it has resolved a technology-related issue that disrupted some departing flights earlier Monday, Anadolu Ajansi reported. "Earlier today, we experienced a technology-related issue that impacted some departing flights. - 'We need brand-new software' Speaking to Fox News, Duffy said Monday that this was not an FAA system-wide problem.

items.title: Costa Rican journalist gunned down near capital
items.summary: SAN JOSE: Costa Rican independent journalist Camilo Rodriguez, who had called out alleged ties between drug traffickers and politicians on social media, was shot dead on Monday outside the capital San Jose, authorities said. Rodriguez, 50, had reported receiving several death threats from drug trafficking groups. He would name drug lords by their full names and claimed to have provided reports to the US Drug Enforcement Administration regarding links between drug traffickers and powerful figures in politics and business.

items.title: Heavy rain, strong winds expected in parts of Perak, Pahang, Sabah
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 17 — Thunderstorms, heavy rain and strong winds are expected to hit several areas in Perak, Pahang and Sabah until 1 pm today. In a statement today, the Malaysian Meteorological Department (MetMalaysia) said the affected areas in Perak are Hulu Perak and Kuala Kangsar, while in Pahang, they involve Pekan and Kuantan. In Sabah, the forecast covers the West Coast (Ranau, Kota Belud, Tuaran and Kota Kinabalu), Sandakan (Telupid, Paitan, Labuk and Sugut, Sandakan and Kinabatangan) and Kudat (Kota Marudu).

items.title: Government to table White Paper on ageing population challenges and opportunities
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Nov 17 — A White Paper on Malaysia’s preparations to become an aged nation is expected to be tabled in the Dewan Rakyat on Dec 2, Economy Minister Akmal Nasrullah Mohd Nasir said. He said Malaysia entered ageing-nation status in 2021 and is expected to become an aged nation by 2048 before reaching super-aged status in 2060. He said plans for this demographic shift should not be viewed solely through the lens of managing senior citizens’ welfare, but must also include equipping future generations for structural changes in the economy and society.

items.title: Flying Doctor Service suspension affects 85 interior Sarawak localities
items.summary: The Health Ministry said, of that number, 16 localities were identified as having no access via alternative land and water transport. Priority is given to localities based on clinical risk, degree of remoteness and the availability of alternative access, the ministry said. For emergency cases during this temporary suspension, the ministry said it ensures every patient receives immediate action based on clinical priority through the emergency medical evacuation (Medevac) service or suitable alternative transport.

items.title: Ismail Lasim: Sorry, but I don't have anything to say right now
items.summary: SEREMBAN: Datuk Ismail Lasim, who resigned as Negri Sembilan menteri besar yesterday, is remaining tightlipped over his and the state's future. Ismail's resignation was confirmed by Barisan Nasional secretary-general Datuk Seri Dr Zambry Abd Kadir yesterday. (https://www.nst.com.my/news/nation/2026/11/1579249/ismail-resigns-negri-sembilan-mb) He had said Ismail had sent his resignation letter to Yang di-Pertuan Besar Tuanku Muhriz Tuanku Munawir, adding that BN chairman Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi had received a copy.

items.title: MetMalaysia: Thunderstorms, strong winds until 1pm in Perak, Pahang, Sabah
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Thunderstorms, heavy rain and strong winds are expected to hit several areas in Perak, Pahang and Sabah until 1pm today. In a statement today, the Malaysian Meteorological Department (MetMalaysia) said the affected areas in Perak are Hulu Perak and Kuala Kangsar, while in Pahang, they are Pekan and Kuantan. In Sabah, the forecast covers the West Coast (Ranau, Kota Belud, Tuaran and Kota Kinabalu), Sandakan (Telupid, Paitan, Labuk and Sugut, Sandakan and Kinabatangan) and Kudat (Kota Marudu).

items.title: KLCC oversupply masks growing demand for premium homes, says Paramount
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Despite a softening property market and concerns over oversupply in Kuala Lumpur, Paramount Corp Bhd remains confident in the resilience of the city's high-end residential segment, underpinned by rising regional wealth, stronger foreign buyer interest and growing demand for larger homes in prime urban locations. While the oversupply situation in Kuala Lumpur, particularly around the KLCC area, has become slightly more pronounced in 2026, Paramount believes the market needs to be viewed through a more differentiated lens. He said the company takes a highly research-driven approach before embarking on any development, carefully assessing the underlying demand and buyer profile for each project.

items.title: 89pct of private health facilities display medicine prices
items.summary: Of the total, 3,905 premises (65.2 per cent) achieved a satisfactory level of price display, while 649 (10.8 per cent) had yet to display medicine prices. Community pharmacies recorded the highest satisfactory rate at 73.1 per cent, involving 2,628 of 3,595 premises. Private hospitals followed at 61.4 per cent (78 of 127), while private medical clinics recorded 57.2 per cent (972 of 1,699).

items.title: US$14bil arms sale 'up to' Trump, Taiwan official says
items.summary: TAIPEI: The timing of Washington's US$14 billion arms sales package to Taiwan is "very much up to" President Donald Trump and will not be affected by the US midterm results, according to a Taiwanese government official. "When it comes to time, I think it's very much up to... President Trump," said Deputy Foreign Minister Chen Ming-chi. Taiwan enjoys "very strong bipartisan support" from Congress, and this month's midterm results, which saw Democrats win control of the House and Senate, would not affect the timing, Chen said.

items.title: Australia to make backpackers do extra rural work to meet labour crunch
items.summary: SYDNEY: Australia said on Tuesday it will require tourists on working holiday visas to complete extra work in rural areas, as the government attempts to balance a reduction in migration with a shortage of labour in its farming and hospitality sectors. Rural employers in Australia are heavily reliant on backpackers to fill seasonal roles. Under the programme for 18-to-35-year-olds, Australia grants a one-year working holiday visa, extendable for a second and third year if the backpackers undertake regional work.

items.title: Malaysia investment approvals jump 20.7pct to RM350.4bil in nine months
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysia has attracted RM350.4 billion in approved investments across the services, manufacturing and primary sectors in the first nine months of 2026, up 20.7 per cent from RM290.3 billion a year earlier. Foreign investments accounted for RM212.3 billion, or 60.6 per cent of total approvals, while domestic investments stood at RM138.1 billion. China followed with RM38.6 billion, Singapore RM38.5 billion, Japan RM24.4 billion and Australia RM12.6 billion.

items.title: Trump, Li Qiang, Modi join Asean leaders as Philippines hosts summit finale
items.summary: MANILA: The Philippines takes centre stage as Asean leaders and key global figures gather for crucial talks on the final day of the 49th Asean Summit. United States President Donald Trump is scheduled to arrive in Manila at 5.30pm local time, making him the last world leader scheduled to arrive for the summit. The 29th Asean-Japan Summit is scheduled for 11.15am, followed by the 13th Mekong-Japan Summit at 12.30pm and the 23rd Asean-India Summit at 1.15pm.

items.title: Malaysia's construction sector builds on growth momentum
items.summary: Construction work done rose 9.0 per cent year-on-year to RM49.5 billion in the quarter, marking the 15th consecutive quarter of expansion, MBSB Research said, based on the Department of Statistics data. Non-residential buildings recorded the strongest growth, rising 21.1 per cent to RM15.7 billion, while special trades increased 13.2 per cent to RM6.2 billion. The private sector remained the main growth driver, with construction work done rising 12.7 per cent to RM33.3 billion, compared with a 2.2 per cent expansion in public-sector activity.

items.title: US chip curbs put data centre projects in focus
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysia's construction players with heavy exposure to data centre projects could face greater uncertainty following tighter United States (US) restrictions on advanced artificial intelligence (AI) chips, although existing projects are unlikely to be derailed immediately. SunCon's outstanding data centre works were estimated at RM10.5 billion to RM11 billion, equivalent to 78-82 per cent of its RM13.4 billion order book. IJM's remaining data centre works were estimated at RM1.8 billion to RM2.2 billion, representing 12 to 15 per cent of its RM14.5 billion order book.

items.title: MARKET PULSE AM NOV 17, 2026 [WATCH]
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Bursa Malaysia opened lower as tighter US licensing rules for advanced AI chips raised concerns over the outlook for Malaysia's data centre sector. In the crypto market, Bitcoin plunged to RM265,961. vmXi06m63wM © New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

items.title: Macron accorded state welcome at Dataran Merdeka
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: French President Emmanuel Macron, who is on a two-day official visit to Malaysia beginning yesterday, was accorded a state welcome at Dataran Merdeka here this morning. Macron, accompanied by his wife Brigitte Macron, arrived at 9.30am and was received by Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim and his wife, Datin Seri Dr Wan Azizah Wan Ismail. Also present were both Deputy Prime Ministers, Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi and Datuk Seri Fadillah Yusof.

items.title: BMI: Higher living costs set to squeeze Malaysian households’ purchasing power
items.summary: BMI said consumers are likely to encounter a more challenging spending environment next year after revising its inflation forecast for Malaysia to 2.0 per cent from 1.8 per cent previously. The research house forecast real GDP growth to slow to 5.2 per cent year-on-year in the third quarter from 6.0 per cent in the preceding quarter, citing mixed high-frequency economic indicators. According to the report, export growth strengthened from 45.5 per cent year-on-year in June to 54.5 per cent in September, while retail sales growth moderated from 4.2 per cent in June to 3.8 per cent in August.

items.title: Malaysians lost RM6.95b to online scams since 2023, Home Ministry says
items.summary: Losses in 2023 totalled RM1.22 billion, rising to RM1.57 billion in 2024 and RM2.97 billion in 2025,” he said. Between January and August 2026, victims lost RM1.18 billion, the reply added. From January to August 2026, police logged another 45,683 cases, Saifuddin said.

items.title: Shell's Rosmari-Marjoram gas fields start production
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Sarawak Shell Bhd has started production from the Rosmari and Marjoram gas fields located 220 kilometres off the coast of Sarawak. Shell upstream president Perer Costello said the company is proud of its long and successful history in Malaysia. Shell drilled Malaysia's first oil well in 1910 and has been producing gas offshore since 1982.

items.title: CAP warns of rising old-age poverty risk
items.summary: GEORGE TOWN: Low wages, inadequate retirement savings and rising living costs are leaving retirees financially vulnerable, with the risk of old-age poverty growing, the Consumers' Association of Penang (CAP) has warned. CAP president Mohideen Abdul Kader said the country needed to overhaul its retirement, healthcare and wage policies to prepare for the challenges of an ageing population. As a result, many older people were increasingly dependent on their children, public healthcare and government assistance, he said.

items.title: Royal assent needed before MB resignation takes effect, says Palace
items.summary: SEREMBAN, Nov 17 — The Negeri Sembilan Palace has clarified that Datuk Ismail Lasim remains Menteri Besar pending royal assent, stressing that any resignation only takes effect after it is accepted by the Yang Dipertuan Besar of Negeri Sembilan in accordance with the state constitution. In a statement today, the palace said it had taken note of a statement issued by Barisan Nasional secretary-general Datuk Seri Zambry Abd Kadir on Nov 16 regarding Ismail's purported resignation from the post. The palace said the statement appeared to be based on a copy of a resignation letter that was in Zambry's possession.

items.title: Japan scrambles jets after two suspected Russian aircraft enter airspace
items.summary: TOKYO: Japan said on Tuesday it scrambled fighter jets after two suspected Russian aircraft violated its airspace, and lodged a "very stern protest" with Moscow. The aircraft entered Japan's airspace close to Okinoshima, in the southwestern area of Fukuoka, shortly after 4am on Tuesday (1900 GMT Monday). Japan's Self-Defence Force scrambled fighter jets to warn the planes, top government spokesman Minoru Kihara said.

items.title: Lim Guan Eng: Indonesia must pay for haze losses or permit regional firefighting force
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 17 — DAP chairman Lim Guan Eng has urged Indonesia to either compensate Malaysia for losses arising from this year’s haze crisis or agree to the formation of a permanent trans-boundary firefighting task force with the authority to enter Indonesian forests immediately to combat fires. In a statement today, Lim said Malaysia should accept the apology offered by Indonesian President Prabowo Subianto to Malaysia and Singapore over the prolonged haze episode in the spirit of good neighbourly relations and ASEAN solidarity. Lim claimed that Malaysia had suffered welfare losses of RM8 billion linked to health impacts and economic losses of RM5 billion as a result of the haze.

items.title: Malayan Flour earnings recovery set to continue
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Malayan Flour Mills Bhd is expected to sustain its earnings recovery, supported by improved flour milling efficiency, favourable input costs and stronger margins in its integrated poultry business. Hong Leong Investment Bank Bhd (HLIB) analyst Chye Wen Fei said the company's earnings prospects remained positive. "We remain constructive of Malayan Flour's earnings prospects, underpinned by improved operating efficiency at its flour milling operations in Malaysia and Vietnam, favourable input cost dynamics within its flour milling operations and margin expansion at the integrated poultry segment," she said in a note.

items.title: Poor students increasingly lured into mule account schemes
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 17 — Online scam syndicates are increasingly exploiting financially vulnerable university and college students by recruiting them as mule account holders, sometimes offering payments of as little as RM40. “These are modern-day mule account tactics. Hishamuddin said students seeking financial aid were also vulnerable.

items.title: Penang Hospital services unaffected by ambulance fire
items.summary: GEORGE TOWN: Operations at Penang Hospital's Emergency and Trauma Department remain unaffected following a fire involving a Civil Defence Force ambulance. The Penang Health Department said medical services continued as normal. The fire broke out after the ambulance crew had transferred an emergency patient to the department.

items.title: Former Negeri Sembilan MB asks for space, says no media statement for now
items.summary: SEREMBAN, Nov 17 — Journalists have gathered at several locations, including the Menteri Besar’s office here, as they await further developments in the political crisis in Negeri Sembilan. This follows Datuk Ismail Lasim’s resignation as Negeri Sembilan Menteri Besar yesterday. Yesterday, Barisan Nasional (BN) secretary-general Datuk Seri Dr Zambry Abd Kadir said BN chairman and UMNO president Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi had received a copy of Ismail’s resignation letter submitted to the Yang Dipertuan Besar of Negeri Sembilan, Tuanku Muhriz Tuanku Munawir.

items.title: Malaysia has 133,400 registered Rohingya refugees and asylum seekers
items.summary: Home Minister Datuk Seri Saifuddin Nasution Ismail said 6,294 Rohingya were being held at immigration detention depots nationwide as at Oct 31. They accounted for part of the 11,208 Myanmar nationals in detention, based on Immigration Department records. "As at Oct 31, a total of 12,176 Myanmar nationals had been repatriated this year, including 1,476 detainees sent home on Sept 29 in a large-scale operation aboard a Myanmar Navy vessel.

items.title: Government cannot terminate Pan Borneo contracts at will, warns Nanta
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 17 — The government could face legal action and damage claims if it arbitrarily terminates contracts awarded to contractors for the Sabah Pan Borneo Highway (LPB) project without following established procedures and legal requirements. Works Minister Datuk Seri Alexander Nanta Linggi said contract termination was not a decision that could be taken lightly, as contractors had legal rights, including the right to apply for an Extension of Time (EOT) if project delays were caused by factors beyond their control. These include delays in site handovers arising from the government’s failure to finalise compensation payments for land acquisition.

items.title: ‘Show me one plot in KL with no value’: Dr Akmal Saleh challenges Hannah Yeoh over RM4.67m land premium
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 17 — Umno Youth chief Datuk Dr Akmal Saleh has challenged Minister in the Prime Minister’s Department (Federal Territories) Hannah Yeoh to identify any parcel of land in Kuala Lumpur that has no value, amid questions over the reduction of a land premium from RM4.67 million to RM1,000. In a Facebook post, Akmal argued that the land belonging to the Kuala Lumpur and Selangor Chinese Assembly Hall (KLSCAH) retained its value despite claims that it had no commercial potential. Akmal also challenged Hannah to identify even a single plot of land in Kuala Lumpur that genuinely had no value.

items.title: Thai drug haul: Two of five arrested Malaysians linked to previous narcotics offences
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 17 — Two of the five Malaysian men arrested by Thai authorities on suspicion of smuggling 240 kilogrammes (kg) of methamphetamine last Wednesday were found to have previous drug-related criminal records. Bukit Aman Narcotics Criminal Investigation Department (NCID) director Datuk Hussein Omar Khan said the suspects, aged 37 and 39, from Kedah, had three and one previous narcotics-related offences respectively. “The three other men, aged 34, 38 and 40, had no drug-related criminal records,” he said when contacted.

items.title: Malaysia proposes new funding sources for Asean haze mitigation efforts
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 17 — Malaysia has proposed that the potential involvement of the agriculture, insurance sectors and health-related entities be explored to strengthen funding efforts to address transboundary haze pollution at the Asean level. The Natural Resources and Environmental Sustainability Ministry said the proposal is in line with Article 20 of the Asean Agreement on Transboundary Haze Pollution (AATHP). “Potential funding sources include international organisations, regional financial institutions, donor agencies and other agreed stakeholders,” the ministry said in a written reply in the Dewan Rakyat to Datuk Seri Tuan Ibharim Tuan Man (PN-Kubang Kerian) yesterday.

items.title: Sri Muda floodgate expected to resume automatic operations within six weeks
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 17 — The electricity supply issue that has resulted in the Sri Muda floodgate in Shah Alam, Selangor, being operated manually is expected to be resolved within six weeks, said Kota Raja Member of Parliament Datuk Seri Mohamad Sabu. Mohamad, who is also Agriculture and Food Security Minister, said resolving the issue was important to enable the floodgate to resume automatic operations. Mohamad said flood management went beyond monitoring water levels and ensuring floodgates functioned efficiently, as it also involved safeguarding the lives, homes and livelihoods of thousands of residents.

items.title: Malaysia retains seat on ITU Council for second consecutive term
items.summary: The Malaysian Communications and Multimedia Commission (MCMC), in a statement today, said the re-election reflected the continued confidence of ITU member states in Malaysia’s contributions and role in advancing digital development internationally. For the 2027-2030 term, MCMC said Malaysia would adopt a more comprehensive approach to bridging the digital divide by going beyond internet connectivity to expand access and strengthen digital skills, ensuring that developing countries could also benefit from emerging technologies. “Malaysia will also champion online safety, digital trust and cybersecurity resilience.

items.title: No new deadline set for South China Sea code negotiations, says Anwar
items.summary: MANILA, Nov 17 — Asean and China have not set a new deadline for concluding negotiations on the South China Sea Code of Conduct (COC), although both sides have reaffirmed their commitment to expediting the process, Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said. He said Asean leaders and Chinese Premier Li Qiang acknowledged the progress made in the negotiations during the Asean-China Summit here yesterday. Asked whether the talks could extend beyond the original end-2026 target, Anwar said he believed they could, given the progress achieved so far.

items.title: Anwar praises Philippines’ stewardship of Asean summit
items.summary: MANILA, Nov 17 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim has praised the Philippines’ Asean chairmanship this year, particularly for ensuring substantive discussions on various issues of regional importance. Anwar leads the Malaysian delegation to the 49th Asean Summit and Related Summits from Nov 15 to 17 under the Philippines’ chairmanship, themed “Navigating Our Future, Together”. He said a more significant development was the growing commitment among Asean member states to further strengthen regional cooperation despite differences in views.

items.title: Man jailed, caned for posing as Selangor Crown Prince's aide in celebrity scam
items.summary: Magistrate Amirul Asyraf Abdul Rasid handed down the sentence on Al Zulfadly Alias, 40, after he pleaded guilty to the charge. His fiancée, Nurul Nur Syahirah Kamarudin, 37, who was charged with the same offence, pleaded not guilty. Deputy Public Prosecutor Nurul Farhanah Arul Hisham sought an appropriate sentence for Al Zulfadly, while Nurul Nur Syahirah was initially offered bail of RM5,000 with one surety.

items.title: Appeals Court upholds dismissal of medical negligence suit against Penang General Hospital
items.summary: PUTRJAJAYA, Nov 17 — The Court of Appeal today dismissed an appeal by a religious teacher in a medical negligence suit against the Malaysian government, medical personnel and staff of the Penang General Hospital, where he was treated after a road accident. A three-member bench comprising Justices Datuk Dr Shahnaz Sulaiman, Datuk Nadzarin Wok Nordin and Datuk Amarjeet Singh today unanimously dismissed and ordered Mohammad Nabill Sajid Mohammad Aslam Sajid to pay RM30,000 as cost. She said in medical damages cases, the applicable standard is that of a reasonable and competent medical practitioner.

items.title: Anwar: China to boost AI technology transfer, training for Asean
items.summary: MANILA, Nov 17 — China has agreed to strengthen cooperation with Malaysia and other Asean member states in the field of artificial intelligence (AI), encompassing aspects of technology transfer and additional training, said Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim. He said that AI and cybersecurity were also major focuses during discussions with dialogue partners at the 49th Asean Summit and Related Summits here. “Both measures could boost intra-Asean trade, with harmonised customs declarations allowing member states to cross-check trade information,” Johari said.

items.title: No reshuffle: Government stable, Cabinet working well, says Anwar
items.summary: MANILA, Nov 17 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim has reaffirmed that the government remains stable and is fully focused on implementing policies and fulfilling its responsibilities to the people rather than entertaining speculation about a Cabinet reshuffle. He said there was no pressing need to reshuffle the Cabinet at present, despite various views emerging following DAP secretary-general Anthony Loke’s resignation as Transport Minister. On Loke’s resignation, Anwar said he respected the DAP leader’s principled stance, although he had earlier asked him to reconsider his decision.

items.title: Negeri Sembilan MB Ismail Lasim resigns
items.summary: SEREMBAN, Nov 17 — Datuk Ismail Lasim has resigned as the Menteri Besar of Negeri Sembilan, said Barisan Nasional (BN) Secretary-General Datuk Seri Zambry Abd Kadir. Zambry said that BN Chairman and UMNO President Datuk Seri Ahmad Zahid Hamidi received a copy of the resignation letter, which was addressed and sent to the Yang Dipertuan Besar of Negeri Sembilan, Tuanku Muhriz Tuanku Munawir, yesterday. Accordingly, he said Ahmad Zahid will submit proposed candidates for the new Menteri Besar to be presented before Tuanku Muhriz in line with the provisions of the Negeri Sembilan State Constitution (UUTKNS).

items.title: Quartz ridges, ivory tusks and ‘perahu payang’: How four flagship ECRL stations celebrate local heritage and geography
items.summary: The ITT Gombak ECRL Station draws inspiration from the Gombak Selangor Quartz Ridge, a geological landmark. — Picture courtesy of Malaysia Rail Link At the western gateway, ITT Gombak takes its design cues from the nearby Gombak Selangor Quartz Ridge, previously known as the Klang Gates Quartz Ridge. The KotaSAS ECRL Station draws inspiration from Pahang's longstanding relationship with elephants.

items.title: Selangor identifies 56 flood hotspots ahead of Northeast Monsoon
items.summary: Selangor Fire and Rescue Department (JBPM) assistant director (Operations) Ashrul Riezal Ashbar said the two main rivers contributing to overflow in the area were Sungai Damansara and Sungai Buluh. Klang has the highest number of flood hotspots, with 13, followed by Petaling (11), Gombak (10), Hulu Langat (nine), Kuala Selangor (six), Sepang (three), and Kuala Langat and Hulu Selangor with two each. Hulu Langat has the highest number of flood-prone areas at 37, followed by Klang (33), Sepang (32), Kuala Selangor and Gombak (29 each), Petaling (27), Kuala Langat (22), Hulu Selangor (12) and Sabak Bernam (11).

items.title: Pasir Gudang MP hands over phone as police probe viral poem
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 16 — Pasir Gudang Member of Parliament Hassan Abdul Karim gave his statement at Bukit Aman today regarding his poem titled Patik Tak Rela which went viral on social media. He arrived at the police headquarters at 2:50 pm to give his statement to the Royal Malaysia Police (PDRM) Classified Criminal Investigation Unit (USJT), with the recording of his statement conducted by the investigating officer starting at 3:00 pm. “I gave my full cooperation and answered nearly 20 questions posed throughout the investigation session,” he said when met by reporters after finishing his statement.

items.title: Dentist fined RM70,000 over use of unregistered staff for dental work
items.summary: PETALING JAYA, Nov 16 — A dentist was fined RM70,000 by the Sessions Court here today after being found guilty of two charges of employing an individual who was not registered as a dental practitioner and allowing the person to perform dental procedures at her clinic two years ago. Dr Tong Soo Huan, 38, was charged with employing an individual who was not registered as a dental practitioner under the Dental Act 2018 at a dental clinic in Jalan SS21/1 here at 12.50 pm on May 6, 2024. The inspection found that the staff member was not registered with the Malaysian Dental Council (MDC) as a dental practitioner, while Dr Tong, who was a registered dental practitioner, failed to produce the staff member’s annual practising certificate when requested by the enforcement officers.

items.title: Two held as KPDN confiscates 27,000 hair dye products bearing suspected unauthorised halal logo
items.summary: TASEK GELUGOR, Nov 16 — The Penang branch of the Domestic Trade and Cost of Living Ministry (KPDN) seized 27,000 bottles of hair dye products worth RM1.08 million suspected of misusing the Malaysian halal logo without a valid Malaysian Halal Certification (SPHM) in a raid on a warehouse in Kampung Selamat here today. "Preliminary investigations found that the products were suspected of displaying the Malaysian halal logo although the company failed to produce valid halal certification documents to substantiate the use of the logo,” he told a media conference at the warehouse here today. He said the company's modus operandi included displaying suspected fake halal certificates in advertisements on social media and e-commerce platforms, as well as engaging popular social media influencers and affiliate agents to convince consumers of the products' halal status.
